The result in Ashhacker was to require the FCC to hold an on-the-record

Ashhacker, however, did not tell the agency what kind of hearing to conduct. 
In fact, in co-channel cases like Ashhacker involving different communities, the 
FCC hearing does not now involve a full-blown comparison of the competing 
broadcasters, but only of the service needs of the respective communities. The 
FCC holds comparative hearings regarding broadcaster merits only for same-

stations and other noncommercial educational broadcasters. Otherwise, the 
FCC is now directed by statute to deal with mutuahy exclusive apphcations for 
initial hcenses or construction permits through a system of competitive

Ashhacker is a limited exception to the general principle that third parties 
cannot demand hearings to determine someone else’s legal rights. Courts have

1997) (holding that no comparative hearing was required where the granting

2. THE PROCEDURES USED TO ADJUDICATE
The APA suggests two categories of adjudicative procedure: (1) 
informal adjudication that does not involve an “on-the-record” hearing and 
is subject only to the misceUaneous provisions of §§ 555 and 558; and (2) 
formal hearings, conducted according to the minimum procedures
